findings.source_passage: But Faith, like a jackal, feeds among the tombs, and even from these dead doubts she gathers her most vital hope.
findings.source_locator: paragraph after the 'All these things are not without their meanings' paragraph
findings.why_it_matters: This is one of the most quoted single sentences in Melville; it is present in the draft but formatted as a quotation block identical to the surrounding analytical paragraphs, stripping its rhetorical isolation and punch as a one-sentence paragraph — the sentence-shape IS the signature.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore as its own isolated paragraph, unquoted, preserving its dramatic severance from the preceding meditation.

findings.source_passage: wherefore but the rumor of a knocking in a tomb will terrify a whole city. All these things are not without their meanings.
findings.source_locator: the long rhetorical-question paragraph, final clause
findings.why_it_matters: The draft includes this but omits the middle rhetorical questions (the Life Insurance Companies paying death-forfeitures upon immortals; antique Adam in unstirring paralysis; why we refuse to be comforted for those dwelling in bliss), gutting the cumulative rhetorical buildup that gives the passage its interpretive weight on mortality and faith.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least two of the omitted rhetorical clauses (especially 'why the Life Insurance Companies pay death-forfeitures upon immortals' and 'in what eternal, unstirring paralysis… antique Adam') to preserve the passage's accumulative logic.

findings.source_passage: In fact take my body who will, take it I say, it is not me. And therefore three cheers for Nantucket
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'take my body who will, take it I say, it is not me' is the interpretive hinge of the closing—Ishmael's bravado rests on this metaphysical claim; the draft jumps directly to 'three cheers' without it, erasing the logical ground for the defiance.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert 'In fact take my body who will, take it I say, it is not me' before 'three cheers for Nantucket' to restore the philosophical warrant for the closing flourish.

findings.source_passage: As well might those tablets stand in the cave of Elephanta as here.
findings.source_locator: end of the 'Oh! ye whose dead' paragraph
findings.why_it_matters: This closing line of the lament paragraph is rhetorically and culturally distinctive—the Elephanta reference marks Melville's exotic-comparative register and seals the paragraph's argument; its absence flattens the paragraph's conclusion.
findings.suggested_fix: Append 'As well might those tablets stand in the cave of Elephanta as here' to close the lament passage.

findings.source_passage: Queequeg… there was a wondering gaze of incredulous curiosity in his countenance.
findings.why_it_matters: The specific detail of Queequeg's 'wondering gaze of incredulous curiosity' characterizes him in contrast to the literate mourners; its loss slightly thins the characterization scene.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a brief phrase capturing Queequeg's expression of wondering curiosity when describing his presence near the door.

summary: The draft preserves much verbatim text but contains one high-severity formatting/isolation failure on the jackal sentence and three medium-severity losses—the gutted rhetorical-question paragraph, the missing 'take my body who will' interpretive hinge, and the absent Elephanta closing line—triggering regeneration.
